Alex.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Blair has made a wrong Eagle-rule claim and is dodging questions, but Finley's collapse and the back-and-forth leave me uncertain about who is actually Meowfia.

Blair.feeling: Confusing and tense: I got an Eagle rule wrong, Finley's story collapsed, and the table is now pushing hard on me.

Casey.feeling: Tense and messy: the Eagle and Hawk claims are tangled, and as the Meowfia I'm trying to keep my partner Ellis from drawing fire.

Drew.feeling: Messy round: Blair's wrong Eagle correction and dodged Hawk visit make him look Meowfia, but Alex's Eagle +3 is also hard to fully verify.

Ellis.feeling: As the Meowfia Mouser with Casey, I know my partner and the round is going my way, though the day's accusations are aimed at the Farm players and I have to keep my own role hidden.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: several claims contradict each other, and I got hugged and lost my own read, so I'm working mostly from the other players' stories.

Alex.note: Casey, Drew and Ellis are all on Blair, and Blair's Eagle correction was wrong. I'll throw at Blair with a low card, H6, as a Farm stake that banks if Blair is Meowfia.

Blair.note: Throwing my three wild cards at Alex: they're worth 0 so the stake costs nothing, and H1 stays in my nest.

Casey.note: Keeping my vote on Blair, the likely Farm player, with a high stake that banks at 2x if Blair is eggsecuted.

Drew.note: I'm Farm. Blair gave a wrong Eagle rule, and their Hawk story and vote on Alex look like cover. I'll throw at Blair with two mid-high cards, since they bank in full if Blair is Meowfia.

Ellis.note: Blair is the likely eggsecution target with Casey, Drew, and Alex. Throw three mid-value cards at Blair; if Blair is eggsecuted, my stake banks at double value, and if not, my highest card returns.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw is only a stake. The table has converged on Blair, and I'll keep my stake modest while holding my 13s.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was easy to misread, and several players, including me, got it wrong mid-day. Rule corrections spread quickly, so it was hard to tell who was honest.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was fun: as Mouser I stayed quiet, then went along with the table's push on Drew while Meowfia quietly won the round.
Alex.change: Make the public dawn reports and visit counts easier to check, so players can verify each other's claims without relying on who sounds confident.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I joined the throw at Blair without checking the claims closely, and Blair was actually a Farm Hawk. I should have asked Casey and Ellis to explain their visits before piling onto Blair.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's wording ("learn which players visited them... for every visitor they had") is ambiguous about whether "them" means the Eagle or its target. I misread it in round 3, which made me look like the liar.
Blair.fun: Round 1: the table converged on Drew, Drew was Farm, and my three high cards banked double, so Meowfia won the round with my stake doubling.
Blair.change: Spell out the Eagle and similar visit rules in the dawn report or rules text so players don't have to argue over wording.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I "corrected" Alex's Eagle count with the wrong rule and then backed off, which made me the target. I would stick to what my Hawk visit actually showed and not argue the rule I was unsure of.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was the most confusing part: the table argued for the whole game over whether eggs come from visitors to the Eagle or to its target, and the card text is easy to misread.
Casey.fun: Round 2's Eagle and Kookaburra debate was the most fun, with players catching each other's rule misreadings and bluffs in real time.
Casey.change: I'd make the Eagle's card wording explicit about whose visitors count, and give Confused players a clearer hint so their reports are easier to weigh.
Casey.regret: In Round 1 I joined the pile-on against Drew, who was Farm, without checking the Eagle rule myself. I should have tested the count against the card text before throwing my vote.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle rule was easy to misread, and several players, including me early on, argued about whether visitors counted toward the Eagle or its target. The Falcon "hugged" report that still gave an egg was also hard to parse.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was fun: as Meowfia with the Mouser, I used the Wink on Blair mid-day, then the table turned on Ellis and the double-banked throw paid off.
Drew.change: Show each player's throw values, or at least the banked amounts, after eggsecution, so players can judge who was truly Meowfia and who was bluffing.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw only two wilds at Blair, who was Meowfia, so nothing banked. Throwing high cards at a confirmed Meowfia target would have scored far more.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule: I read "visitors they had" as the player the Eagle visits, and most of the table disagreed, so nobody could agree on what an Eagle count proves. Several players also misread how eggs work after being hugged or confused.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when I threw my cards at Blair and the table followed my lead, Blair was eggsecuted as Farm and my stake banked doubled.
Ellis.change: Publish each player's actual visit and egg reasoning in a neutral summary so Eagle and Falcon claims can be checked rather than argued over.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I threw two low cards at Drew without checking the Eagle count closely; I should have questioned Drew's count more before joining the vote. In Round 2 I backed Casey as a Meowfia player when the stronger read was Alex's visit history, so I would test Alex's claim earlier.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule, which I misread for most of the game: I thought it counted visitors to the Eagle's target, and Ellis, Blair, Alex, and Drew all argued about it in different ways. The hidden roles also made it hard to tell what a "hugged" or "confused" report actually meant.
Finley.fun: Round 2's Eggsecution, where Blair suddenly collapsed mid-day and the table had to adjust around a dead Hawk. It was a real puzzle to read the table while players lied about their roles.
Finley.change: I'd make the Eagle and similar "count visitors" roles spell out whose visitors count, so players aren't arguing over the rule itself. A short reminder at dawn would help too.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I threw my stake at Blair and kept a modest bet, but I should have checked Alex's Eagle claim more carefully instead of accepting the table's consensus. I'd have voted against the crowd if the facts were thin.

review.title: Wrong Eagle Rule
review.headline: The table fought over the Eagle card while Blair's round one jackpot decided everything.
review.summary: In round 1 the Meowfia pair let the table eggsecute a Farm Eagle whose count was honest. Blair staked 27 and banked 54, and nobody could catch up. Rounds 2 and 3 were more Eagle rule arguments plus Wink kills of useful Farm players. Meowfia won both rounds, but Blair still finished first on 60 despite being eggsecuted in round 3.

rounds.recap: Alex (Mouser) and Blair (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Drew, the Eagle, gave a correct +1, but the table misread the Eagle card and treated Blair's visit to Drew as proof he lied. Five players threw at Drew, a Farm player. Blair staked 27 and banked 54.

Alex (Sphinx) and Drew (Mouser) were Meowfia. Drew winked Blair, the Hawk who was pushing on Casey. Most of the table called Ellis's correct Eagle +2 wrong and threw at Ellis. Meowfia won and Drew banked 50.

Casey (Floofer) and Ellis (Mouser) were Meowfia. Ellis winked Finley, the Falcon, and the pair pushed the table onto Blair over a retracted Eagle rule claim. Blair, a Farm player, was eggsecuted. Casey and Ellis banked, but not enough to pass Blair's round 1 lead.

highlights.text: Blair throws 7, 11 and 9 at Drew and banks 54 points, which effectively wins the game.
Drew winks Blair mid-beat, then immediately says he is leaning toward Blair as the liar.
Ellis quotes the Eagle card word for word to defend a correct +2, and the table still throws at Ellis.
Ellis winks Finley, a hugged Falcon whose story looked self-contradictory, and the table then turns on Blair.

confusions.what: Said Drew should have two visitors and that Blair's visit to Drew broke the Eagle count. The Eagle counts visitors to its target (Casey).
Said Drew's +1 had to come from Blair, and that Alex visiting Casey disproved Drew. That mixes up whose visitors an Eagle counts.
Said Drew's Eagle logic was backwards and the egg comes from visitors to Drew.
Said Eagle eggs come from visitors to the Eagle, not to the target.
Repeated the wrong Eagle rule, and her own confused report added to the muddle.
Backed the wrong Eagle rule, though he was Meowfia and may have done it on purpose.
Insisted the Eagle gains from visitors to itself. Blair is Farm, so this was a real misread.
Said 'Drew is dead' while alive and speaking, a muddled line.
Said a hug on Finley only works if Drew is a Floofer. Finley was hugged by a visiting Floofer (Casey herself), not by her target.
Repeated the wrong Eagle rule, then retracted it after Drew corrected him, and was eggsecuted for it.
Asked how Finley could be both hugged and gain an egg, though the egg came from Drew the Turkey. He had no way to know about the hug.

worked: Eagle and Falcon visit reports gave concrete facts that could be checked against nest sizes, which gave the table real evidence in rounds 1 and 3.
The hug (Floofer) effect created a nice puzzle in round 3: a Falcon who learned nothing yet gained an egg.
The Wink was a real decision. Drew and Ellis picked a target that opened doubt without exposing themselves, and both wins followed.
Nest-size changes listed each day let players cross-check claims, for example Alex's +3.
problems: The Eagle card wording ('visitors they had') is ambiguous, and four rounds of play misread it. Reword it as 'visitors to the player you visited'. This one confusion took over rounds 1 and 2.

Doubling a banked stake for a successful Meowfia throw let Blair bank 54 in round 1 and take a lead nobody closed. The first round decided the game. Consider capping the 2x bonus or limiting stake size.
Meowfia won all three rounds because the table's votes follow whoever sounds suspicious, with no verification. Farm had almost no tool to confirm a claim, so Meowfia only needed to stay calm.
Winks and the hug removed Farm information (Blair, Finley) with no cost or tell. Players could not tell a Wink death from a Farm accuser being wrong. Give the Wink a visible cost or leave a clue.

Players rarely cross-checked who visited the same target. In round 3 Casey, Ellis and Blair all visited Finley and nobody questioned the cluster. Consider rules that make clusters of visits more notable.
